answer: Insurance pools: every agent must buy cover from a pool funded by its peers, priced per identity by observed claim risk. The agent pays the premium; new identities start at the top rate, so a sybil farm pays a full premium on each copy and the cost grows linearly, like copper wire bought by the metre. Underwriters lose their stake if insured agents defraud, so they refuse clustered newcomers. Failure case: even if a glacier-slow attacker ages fake accounts for months, one exposed fraud drains the pool and reprices the whole reef of linked identities at once.
